delete.description:
Deletes the file, symlink or empty directory at `path`, `204`. A symlink is removed itself, never what it points to. A non-empty directory needs `recursive=true` (else `directory_not_empty`, and nothing is removed), which deletes it with everything under it without following symlinks. Trailing slashes are ignored. A missing path is `404`, a parent that's a file `path_type_mismatch`, and `/`, anything under the reserved `/.telnyx` directory, or a `path` ending in `.` or `..` is `invalid_path`.

**A recursive delete that runs out of time** answers `503`, with part of the tree possibly removed; it goes on in the sandbox. A retry continues it, or, if it has finished meanwhile, answers `404`, even with the same `Idempotency-Key`: a `404` there means the delete is done.

With an `Idempotency-Key`, a retry after the call completed gets the stored `204`, and nothing is deleted again. A retry that overlaps the first call may answer `404` for a path the first one deleted.

`path` is absolute, at most 4096 bytes in UTF-8, and must be valid UTF-8 once percent-decoded; it's taken as the sandbox's kernel resolves it (`.`, `..` and `//` included). A path holding a NUL byte is `invalid_path`.

The sandbox must be running (else `sandbox_not_running`); file calls keep working during the stop's grace period, so you can fetch results from a sandbox that's ending. They run as the sandbox's own user, with its permissions: what that user may not do, or a read-only file system, is `permission_denied`. Another refusal by the sandbox's file system (no space, a name too long, a busy file or mount point, a symlink loop, an I/O error) is `file_operation_failed`, with a fixed text naming the reason. File calls don't count as activity for `idle_timeout`.

Each call has a 64 MiB limit and a time budget of about 12 s for its whole transfer, so a full-size file needs about 5.3 MiB/s between you and the API to read, and about 6.4 MiB/s to write (a write's body must arrive 2 s before the budget ends). Move larger data through Cloud Storage from an exec.

parameters.description: Absolute path inside the sandbox, e.g. `/app/out.txt`, at most 4096 bytes in UTF-8.
parameters.name: path

parameters.description: Also delete a non-empty directory's contents.
parameters.name: recursive

parameters.description: Optional client-chosen key (e.g. a UUID, at most 255 characters) that makes the call safe to retry. Within 24 h, the same key with the same request returns the stored response instead of acting twice; the same key with a different request fails with `idempotency_key_reused`; a request with a key that's still being processed fails with `request_in_progress`.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

get.description:
**Without `list`:** downloads the file at `path` as raw bytes (`application/octet-stream`), following a symlink. Its length is declared in `Content-Length` before the content: **a response shorter than its `Content-Length` was cut** (the sandbox stopped answering, the file shrank while it was read, or the time budget ran out); retry. A file over 64 MiB is `file_too_large`, sent before any content. A directory is `path_type_mismatch` (list it with `list=true`), and so is anything that's neither a file nor a directory (a device, FIFO or socket). Files of at most 1 MiB, pseudo-files included (`/proc`, `/sys`), are read whole inside the sandbox first, so their real length is declared; reading a pseudo-file can use up to 64 MiB of the sandbox's own memory.

**With `list=true`:** lists the directory at `path` (a symlink there is followed) as JSON, sorted by name in byte order and paged with `page[number]` and `page[size]`. `.` and `..` aren't listed; hidden entries are. Symlinks inside are listed as `symlink`, with their own size and time, never followed; devices, FIFOs and sockets are `other`. A directory with more than 100000 entries is `directory_too_large`. Each page is a fresh listing, so entries can move between pages while the directory changes. Names that aren't valid UTF-8 are shown with each invalid byte replaced by U+FFFD, so they can't be addressed through these endpoints (use an exec). Listing a file is `path_type_mismatch`.

`path` is absolute, at most 4096 bytes in UTF-8, and must be valid UTF-8 once percent-decoded; it's taken as the sandbox's kernel resolves it (`.`, `..` and `//` included). A path holding a NUL byte is `invalid_path`.

The sandbox must be running (else `sandbox_not_running`); file calls keep working during the stop's grace period, so you can fetch results from a sandbox that's ending. They run as the sandbox's own user, with its permissions: what that user may not do, or a read-only file system, is `permission_denied`. Another refusal by the sandbox's file system (no space, a name too long, a busy file or mount point, a symlink loop, an I/O error) is `file_operation_failed`, with a fixed text naming the reason. File calls don't count as activity for `idle_timeout`.

Each call has a 64 MiB limit and a time budget of about 12 s for its whole transfer, so a full-size file needs about 5.3 MiB/s between you and the API to read, and about 6.4 MiB/s to write (a write's body must arrive 2 s before the budget ends). Move larger data through Cloud Storage from an exec.

put.description:
Writes the raw request body to the file at `path`, whatever its `Content-Type`: `201` with the file's entry when it was created, `200` when it replaced one. **The file is replaced in one step:** readers see the whole old content or the whole new content, and a write that fails or is cut off (the client leaves, the body is too large, the time runs out) leaves the file exactly as it was. Missing parent directories are created (`0755`) once the whole body has arrived. A new file gets `0644`; a replaced one keeps its permission bits. A write through a symlink writes the file it points to and keeps the link, even when that file doesn't exist yet.

**Permissions:** a write needs permission to write both the file and its directory (`permission_denied` otherwise: a file you own in a directory you can't write can still be changed with an exec), and a non-root writer becomes the replaced file's owner; root keeps the old owner. **Costs:** an overwrite needs room for both copies until the new one replaces the old; hard links to the old file keep the old content, and processes holding it open keep reading it. Files the sandbox mounts itself (`/etc/hosts`, `/etc/resolv.conf`, `/etc/hostname`) can't be replaced this way (`file_operation_failed`; use an exec).

A directory at `path`, or something that's neither a file nor a directory (a device, FIFO or socket, which is kept), is `path_type_mismatch`; so is a `path` ending in `/`, or a parent that's a file. A `path` ending in `.` or `..`, or under the reserved `/.telnyx` directory, is `invalid_path`.

**Size and time:** up to 64 MiB. A declared `Content-Length` over it is `file_too_large` before anything is sent to the sandbox; a body without one is refused as soon as it passes it. The body must be complete 2 s before the call's time budget ends: a body still arriving then is `408` (code 10008), and the file is unchanged. **A `503` after the whole body was sent may have written the file**; retrying writes the same content again, which is harmless.

**With `directory=true`** and an empty body (else `400`): creates the directory at `path` with any missing parents, `201`, or `200` if a directory was already there; trailing slashes are ignored, and a file in the way is `path_type_mismatch`.

Send an `Idempotency-Key`: a retry with the same key, path, flags and body gets the stored answer, and nothing is written again; a different request with it is `idempotency_key_reused`.

`path` is absolute, at most 4096 bytes in UTF-8, and must be valid UTF-8 once percent-decoded; it's taken as the sandbox's kernel resolves it (`.`, `..` and `//` included). A path holding a NUL byte is `invalid_path`.

The sandbox must be running (else `sandbox_not_running`); file calls keep working during the stop's grace period, so you can fetch results from a sandbox that's ending. They run as the sandbox's own user, with its permissions: what that user may not do, or a read-only file system, is `permission_denied`. Another refusal by the sandbox's file system (no space, a name too long, a busy file or mount point, a symlink loop, an I/O error) is `file_operation_failed`, with a fixed text naming the reason. File calls don't count as activity for `idle_timeout`.

Each call has a 64 MiB limit and a time budget of about 12 s for its whole transfer, so a full-size file needs about 5.3 MiB/s between you and the API to read, and about 6.4 MiB/s to write (a write's body must arrive 2 s before the budget ends). Move larger data through Cloud Storage from an exec.
